report.tagline: One app for food delivery, 10-minute groceries (Instamart), restaurant table booking and more, tied together by the Swiggy One membership.
report.simpleSummary: Swiggy is an app where you can order food from restaurants, get groceries in about 10 minutes through Instamart, and book a table to eat out. One login and one payment work across all of them. If you pay for Swiggy One, you get free delivery and discounts on food and groceries together. Food delivery makes money; Instamart is growing but still loses a lot.

overview.whatItDoes: Swiggy started in Bengaluru in 2014 as a food delivery app. It now runs food delivery, Instamart (10-minute groceries and essentials), Dineout (table booking and dining discounts), Scenes (events) and low-price meal options like Toing. It listed on the stock market in November 2024. Its big idea is that one customer, one rider fleet and one membership can serve many needs.
howItWorks: Restaurants list on Swiggy and pay a commission on each food order; Swiggy's delivery partners pick up and deliver.
Instamart runs dark stores, small warehouses near homes, and delivers groceries in about 10 to 20 minutes.
The same delivery partner fleet and the same app serve food and Instamart orders.
Swiggy One membership gives free delivery and extra discounts across food and Instamart, so members use more than one service.
Restaurants and brands pay for ads to show up higher in search and lists.
Dineout lets users book tables and pay the bill in the app for a discount, with Swiggy taking a fee from the restaurant.
overview.valueProposition: Everything you need for daily life, from dinner to groceries to a night out, in one app with one membership that saves money across all of it.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Order from restaurants with ratings, filters, live tracking and delivery in about 30 minutes.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: The original, profitable business (₹341 crore EBITDA in Q2 FY27) that funds the rest.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: 10 to 20 minute delivery of groceries, fresh food, electronics, beauty and gifts.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Biggest growth bet; turns Swiggy into a daily-use app, but it still loses money.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: A paid plan with free deliveries and extra discounts across food and Instamart; cheaper One Lite and premium One BLCK versions exist.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Bundling makes members use two or more services, order more and stay longer.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Book tables and pay bills for discounts at restaurants.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Adds a high-margin 'going out' use case without needing riders.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Paid listings and banners in food and Instamart.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: High-margin money that improves profit per order.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Low-price meal menus and the Toing app for budget meals.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Reaches price-sensitive users and smaller order sizes that the main app does not serve well.

businessModel.summary: Swiggy earns commissions from restaurants, fees from customers, margin and fees on Instamart orders, ads from restaurants and brands, and membership fees. Food delivery is profitable. Instamart's losses are bigger than food's profit, so the company as a whole still loses money.

revenueStreams.detail: Restaurants pay a cut of each food order, often around 18-25% (estimate).
Delivery fee, platform fee per order, small-order fee and surge fees in rain or late nights.
Earnings from sellers and brands on goods sold, plus delivery and handling fees.
Restaurants and brands pay for better visibility in search and lists.
Membership fees, Dineout fees from restaurants, events and other small businesses.

businessModel.pricing: Food: menu prices set by restaurants plus a platform fee (around ₹10 to ₹15 per order, changes often), packaging charges and delivery fees for non-members. Instamart: free delivery above a basket limit, fees below it. Swiggy One plans vary by city and offer; One Lite has been sold at about ₹99 for 3 months. Exact current prices not fixed or fully public.
costDrivers: Paying delivery partners for each trip
Instamart dark-store rent, staff and stock wastage
Discounts and marketing to fight Zomato, Blinkit and Zepto
businessModel.unitEconomics: Food: on a ₹450 food order (estimate), Swiggy keeps about ₹100 from restaurant commission, platform fee and ads, its take rate. After paying the rider about ₹50 to ₹60 and discounts and support, it keeps a small profit; food delivery EBITDA was ₹341 crore in Q2 FY27. Instamart: on a ₹550 order (estimate), revenue is similar to Blinkit's but stores are less busy, so fixed costs per order are higher. Instamart lost about ₹85 per order across FY26 (₹3,511 crore loss over 412 million orders). Profit depends on filling stores with more orders and raising ad income.

howTheyGetUsers: Brand marketing and offers in big and mid-sized cities
Cross-selling from food users into Instamart and Dineout
Swiggy One membership and low-cost One Lite plans
Affordable food formats for price-sensitive users
Opening new Instamart stores in new areas
whatBringsUsersBack: Swiggy One savings make members prefer Swiggy over rivals
Personalised restaurant picks and reorder buttons
Saved addresses and payments across all services
growth.moat: Swiggy's moat is its two-sided network in food: lots of restaurants attract users, and lots of users attract restaurants. Its bundle (one membership across food and groceries) is hard for single-service apps to copy. But Zomato has a similar network, and Blinkit is far ahead in quick commerce, so the moat is shared, not unique.

competitors.name: Zomato (Eternal)
competitors.positioning: Food delivery leader with Zomato Gold membership and a larger share of the market.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Swiggy is the number two in food, but has one combined app for food and groceries, while Zomato keeps Blinkit as a separate app.

competitors.name: Blinkit
competitors.positioning: Quick commerce leader with about 46% share and EBITDA profit.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Instamart is about half Blinkit's size by orders and still loses money, but benefits from Swiggy's food users and bundle.

competitors.name: Zepto
competitors.positioning: Fast-growing stand-alone quick commerce app with Zepto Cafe.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Instamart had fewer orders (412 million vs 640 million in FY26) but sits inside a profitable food app.

competitors.name: Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Swiggy has a daily food habit to cross-sell from; the giants have more money and bigger product ranges.

competitors.name: Rapido and ONDC-based apps
competitors.positioning: Newer low-commission food delivery models that charge restaurants less.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Swiggy has more restaurants and users, but faces pressure on commissions from low-fee models.

northStar.metric: Monthly users who order from two or more Swiggy services
northStar.why: Swiggy's value is the bundle. A user who orders food and groceries gets more value, saves more with Swiggy One, and is less likely to leave for a single-service rival.

improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer abandoned carts and better trust.

pmLessons: Bundling only works if each piece is good. A membership cannot save a slow or out-of-stock grocery service.
Use a profitable core to fund a new bet, but set clear limits on how long the bet can lose money.
Cross-sell is a product problem: the second service must be one tap away, with no new setup.
Being number two in two markets is harder than being number one in one.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase the share of Swiggy food users who also use Instamart?
interviewQuestions.hint: Map the funnel from food user to first Instamart order to repeat. Find the biggest drop. Ideas: in-app placements, combined cart, membership benefits. Pick one and define the metric.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Swiggy split Instamart into a separate app like Zomato did with Blinkit?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh cross-sell from one app against focus and speed of a separate app. Look at data on how Instamart users arrive. Consider brand, app clutter and membership.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a new Swiggy One plan for students.
interviewQuestions.hint: Define the user's needs (cheap meals, small orders). Price against savings and cost to Swiggy. Add limits to avoid losses. Track incremental orders and renewal.

interviewQuestions.question: Instamart's orders grew but losses widened. What would you look at?
interviewQuestions.hint: Break loss per order into revenue per order and cost per order. Check new store share, orders per store, discount spend and delivery cost. Decide whether losses come from investment or from a broken model.

interviewQuestions.question: Restaurants complain about high commissions. How would you respond as PM?
interviewQuestions.hint: Understand what restaurants value (orders, visibility). Consider tiered commissions, better tools, or ad credits. Balance restaurant health with Swiggy's take rate.

assumptions: Order sizes (₹450 food, ₹550 Instamart) and commission ranges are estimates, not published figures.
Exact Q2 FY27 revenue varies across reports (₹7,600 to ₹7,900 crore); we give a range.
Instamart loss per order (about ₹85) is our division of FY26 loss by FY26 orders.
Swiggy One prices and platform fees change often; figures shown are recent examples.
